## Outcome and intended use

The declared comparison between gate-passing starts within 1% of the selected cost passes: A1's 88-row Ermatchkov AARD is 26.208496003%, versus 26.208406176% for A3. The absolute difference is 0.0000898275 percentage points, below the non-identification threshold of 2 percentage points or more. B1 has no qualifying alternative: B3 fails the phase gate, and B2 duplicates B1. This check concerns agreement of pressure predictions between starts; it does not establish identification of individual parameters. The [eligibility and comparison record](results/stage2-capped/equal-cost-starts.json) and [88 A1 row predictions](results/stage2-capped/A1/ermatchkov-88.json) retain the numerical evidence.

Variant A fails the declared 24.2% pressure-transfer test; Variant B passes. AARD is average absolute relative deviation. The endpoints were selected by the lowest fitted cost among candidates passing the density-classified phase gate. Selection was committed in `005f79e` before any outside-fit statistic for the new capped endpoints was computed.

| Endpoint | Cost | Ermatchkov AARD (%) | 24.2% test | Dense splits | Gas states | Reconstruction trials | Other unresolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 | 403.7 | 26.21 | Fail | 0 | 39 | 0 | 0 |
| B1 | 374.5 | 19.15 | Pass | 0 | 37 | 0 | 0 |

![Variant A exceeds the declared pressure limit; Variant B is below it. Points are aggregate statistics over 88 retained source rows, not an uncertainty estimate.](results/stage2-capped/transfer-test.png)

The pressure test uses all 88 Ermatchkov rows at ≤49 wt% MDEA, including the 29 rows below 7 kPa. The 13 higher-concentration rows and the complete 33-row low-pressure subset are separate comparisons. Nitrogen headspace is not modeled. These are conditional physical assessments of the declared model against outside-fit data. Fitted errors are calibration evidence; phase searches, derivative comparisons and balances are numerical verification. There is no absorber-use qualification or universal-ion-parameter claim.

## Model, inputs and selection

The liquid contains water, CO₂, MDEA, MDEAH⁺, bicarbonate, carbonate, hydronium and hydroxide; only neutral species enter the vapor. Variant A uses the MEA single-sphere cation convention; Variant B uses the charged-molecule convention. The shared MEA components, interactions and reaction laws remain frozen in the main fits. The MDEA–water interaction is linear in temperature, initialized from the Kim pre-fit. Neumann ideal-gas Cp is primary, with Wangler evaluated at the same endpoints as a sensitivity. Carson is integral heat from zero loading at 101325 Pa; Jakobsen scales are 10% of each observed ratio; Böttinger is evaluated at 5 and 25 bar.

Merkley uses the native Engine observable with final loading equal to the smaller of the digitized loading point and model saturation loading at 1121 kPa (1466 kPa for the 422.04 K source rows). Only the 20/40 wt% rows at 333.15 and 388.71 K enter the objective. The reaction domain remains 293.15–395 K; the 288.71/422.04 K Merkley and 413 K Kuranov comparisons are retained as unevaluated domain refusals. The source-loading digitization uncertainty is ±0.02 mol CO₂/mol MDEA. Above Hsieh's 328.15 K, the dielectric temperature dependence is a model assumption. The intended comparison domain is ≤49 wt% for the pressure test and ≤50 wt% for other properties; 60 wt% is extrapolation.

A1, A3, B1 and B3 all converged. A2/B2 are duplicates, and A4 remains excluded. B3 has one unresolved phase record (`comparison:113:0`) and is inadmissible for selection. A1 and A3 have costs differing by less than 1e-8; the declared exact lowest-cost rule selects A3. Active bounds are accepted under the owner's MEA precedent and do not establish that these quantities are experimentally identified.

| Endpoint | Coordinate | Target | Quantity | Value | Bounds |

| A3 | 2 | MDEAH⁺–CO₂ | k (dimensionless) | 0.5 | [-0.5, 0.5] |

## Saturation truncation and phase search

The phase classifier was declared before refitting: packing fraction above 0.10 is dense; ambiguity near the threshold and other unresolved trials block a clean gate. Gas evolution is reported separately. Zero-loading searches use carbon-free trial supports. Each selected endpoint has 760 state records, including repeated physical states for distinct observables and six formal cap states from the direct saturation diagnostic. Native heat availability is recorded separately. There are zero reconstruction trials, so no residual #904 ion-free recovery is needed. Full state/trial records and hashes are retained, rather than interpreting gas-like liquid seeds as liquid–liquid splitting.

## Bicarbonate follow-up

| Selected start | Bicarbonate-release pressure AARD (%) | Jacobian correlation with cation–water | Control comparison | Control minus bicarbonate (points) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 | 20.73 | 0.9939 | UNAVAILABLE | Unavailable |
| B1 | 32.52 | -0.7357 | UNAVAILABLE | Unavailable |

| Control start | Iteration limit | Termination | Cost | Dense split states | Unresolved states | Outside-fit AARD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 | 40 | converged | 390.5 | 7 | 1 | Not computed |
| B1 | 40 | limit_reached | 365.8 | 2 | 0 | Not computed |
| B1 | 100 | converged | 365.8 | 2 | 1 | Not computed |

The original B control stopped at the declared 40-iteration limit, with 27 retained saturation refusals and cost 365.820961; its phase results describe that finite, unconverged candidate. The owner authorized one fresh run from the same control start with only the iteration limit raised to 100. Its termination is converged, cost 365.820958506, with 34 refused trials. The released MDEA–CO₂ column's cosine correlation with the cation–water column is 0.134571; at a rejected endpoint this is a diagnostic quantity. The B comparison is UNAVAILABLE under the owner's stopping rule; its control outside-fit AARD and the two-point verdict are unavailable. No further run was made.

The owner's 2026-10-29 decision makes a phase-failed CO₂-control comparison unavailable: retain its endpoint, cost and gate states; do not compute its outside-fit AARD and make no bicarbonate claim for that variant. A bicarbonate-release AARD alone is comparison evidence, not a verdict. A magnitude above 0.95 in the declared column correlation means the pair is non-separable. When a control passes, the declared margin is two AARD percentage points, with the other property results retained; corrected Kamps is excluded. No MDEA outcome falsifies the MEA bicarbonate value, whose MEA conditional uncertainty already spans the declared range.

## Engine acceptance and provenance

All new calculations use the isolated worktree MDEA environment with Engine `d513820994a78bfe628d42fffd55b2eeab6f89bd`, immutable wheel SHA-256 `ca7093ca721fdc80226c74d018a582f31705684c6995e80b0492c193334dd5d5`. The main MEA dependency pins remain on 3e83e19c. Exact wheel path, installed-byte verification and runtime identity are in [runtime.json](results/stage2-capped/runtime.json).

Acceptance (a) passes: the historical A1/B1 754-state searches have zero reconstruction trials; every other classification is unchanged; maximum absolute change in ΔG/RT is 1.82e-12, within the owner's clarified 1e-10 absolute criterion near zero. Acceptance (b) passes: eight start values and four branch checks agree with direct saturation-plus-heat within 4.79e-13 relative, and all nine derivatives pass 1e-5 on both branches (worst error across all 72 comparisons and both declared steps 2.17e-6). Acceptance (c) passes: both 61-row Kim laws replay within 9.33e-15 relative, all 2354 binary phase searches and all mixing scans pass, and item-(l) Cp and the eight retained Carson checks pass. See the [acceptance guide](results/stage2-density/engine-d5138209/README.md).

Newly retained files above 5 MB are gzipped with raw/compressed SHA-256 hashes in [the evidence registry](results/compressed-evidence.json). The manuscript and Engine source are unchanged. Historical pre-cap results remain in their existing result directories and Git history; they are not the selected endpoints shown here.



## Additional sources at the frozen endpoints {#sources-225}

Xiao's 20 equilibrium measurements give CO₂ partial-pressure AARDs of **20.40% at A3** and **28.28% at B1** at 23.5 wt% unloaded MDEA and 298.15–313.15 K.
The source is outside the fitted datasets.
These additional-source comparisons change neither the 24.2% Ermatchkov criterion nor its verdict: A fails and B passes.
No parameters were fitted and no manuscript result is revised.

| Source and quantity | Rows | A3 AARD (%) | B1 AARD (%) | Conditions and disposition |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Xiao Table 4, CO₂ partial pressure | 20 | 20.397551 | 28.276415 | 23.5 wt%, 298.15–313.15 K, 8.1–60.8 kPa |
| Ermatchkov primary CO₂ partial pressure, retained #222 statistic | 88 | 26.208406 | 19.146012 | ≤49 wt%; unchanged |
| Zhang equilibrium pressure/loading | 16 conditions | Unscored | Unscored | 5 mol/L single MDEA; extrapolation; numerical loadings and conversion density unavailable |
| Derks Table 1, species concentrations | 4 | Unscored | Unscored | 2 kmol/m³ initial MDEA; numerical temperature unavailable |

For Xiao, the calculation follows the #222 bubble-state pressure path at each measured loading and uses $p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}=P y_{\mathrm{CO_2}}$.
The logarithmic residual is $r_i=\ln(p_{i,\mathrm{model}}/p_{i,\mathrm{observed}})$; the reported AARD is $100 N^{-1}\sum_i |\exp(r_i)-1|$, rather than a percentage of logarithms.
The mean absolute log ratios are 0.239241 at A3 and 0.354606 at B1.
All 20 predictions are available at each endpoint, with requested equilibrium tolerances met.
The unloaded MDEA mass fraction is the printed 0.235; the printed rounded molality 2.58 mol/kg water is retained separately.
The experiments used CO₂/N₂ at 0.101 MPa; the model omits nitrogen, as in the Ermatchkov comparison.
These are conditional model predictions compared with measured pressures, not absorber-use qualification.
Source uncertainty is retained without treating it as parameter uncertainty or propagating it into an AARD confidence interval.

![Frozen endpoint predictions mostly underpredict Xiao's CO₂ partial pressures across the measured loading range. Points show predictions only at measured loadings; observation error bars are the source standard uncertainties, ±0.004 mol/mol loading and 1.5% pressure. Temperature and composition uncertainties are not displayed.](results/context-sources/Xiao-pressure.png)

The same #222 phase search was applied to each scored bubble state: reacting liquid on all eight species, vapor trials on neutral species, packing-fraction threshold 0.10, and the retained ambiguity interval 0.05–0.35.
At A3 and B1 separately, **20/20 states pass**, with **zero dense-split states, zero gas-evolution states, zero ambiguous states and zero unresolved states**.
No support-reconstruction failures occurred.
Gas evolution is counted separately and is not a dense-liquid failure.
These searches provide numerical evidence for the model's phase assumption at the scored states; they do not establish experimental phase stability or exhaustive global stability.
No phase search is claimed for unscored Zhang or Derks states.

The paper's endpoint criterion is loading unchanged for two hours within ±0.002 C/N, with duplicate maximum deviation from the mean below 1%; Table S2 has no per-row uncertainty.
No numerical unloaded-solvent density was found in the main paper or supplement to convert 5 mol/L to mass fraction.
The issue's “about 57 wt%” remains a domain designation, not a substituted conversion datum.
Every prospective Zhang comparison is **extrapolation** beyond the 49/50 wt% domain.
No correlation-generated loadings or assumed density were substituted for observations.

Parent **48VSQYEE**, attachment **5467GXJK**, SHA-256 `b646d4caafe53705d0b064698061f487fdc7f87d6e23908b6b31fb8029738582`, identifies the seven-page PDF.

## Shared bicarbonate sensitivity and the Xiao pressure miss

At the frozen MDEA endpoints, reducing the bicarbonate–water interaction from
$k=0.7270558477497251$ to $0.6270558477497251$ improves Xiao agreement for both
cation representations. It improves the Ermatchkov comparison for the single
sphere A3 but worsens it for charged-molecule B1. The same change raises the
MEA 307-observation weighted cost from 148.879 to 157.930. These are conditional
parameter sensitivities, not an adopted shared value or evidence that the
cation representation alone controls the pressure error.

Xiao Table 4 supplies 20 measurements at 23.5 wt% unloaded analytical MDEA,
298.15–313.15 K and 8.1–60.8 kPa CO₂ partial pressure. The molality calculated
from that mass fraction is 2.57791 mol/kg water, consistent with the printed
2.58. Loading is moles of added CO₂ per mole of analytical MDEA. Section 3.2
and the table footnote identify CO₂/N₂ at 0.101 MPa total pressure. The
calculation retains the existing nitrogen-free bubble state and computes
$P y_{\mathrm{CO_2}}$. It therefore matches the reported quantity's label but
not the experiment's total-pressure state. Nitrogen and this pressure-state
difference remain unresolved; the results do not isolate an intrinsic
physical-model cause for the Xiao miss.

The live full Xiao PDF (Zotero `6H2LM5C5` / `C3NAG687`) matches the retained
SHA-256. Ermatchkov's current reading copy also matches the indexed Zotero
sidecar. Its Experimental Technique and Tables 1–3 establish the molality
basis for the 88 primary comparison rows. [Source checks and input hashes](results/transfer-267/source-basis.json)
record these findings. The four-reaction chemistry retains R1–R3 and the
MDEAH⁺ dissociation direction and reference convention. Uyan 2015 §3 and Table 1
supply the mole-fraction law; its molality conversion adds 4.0165 to $\ln K$.
It gives $pK_m=8.54994$ at 298.15 K, versus 8.55071 from the Kamps–Maurer law.
The [existing source comparison](results/reaction-basis-kamps-maurer.json)
attributes the small difference to printed coefficient rounding. Application
above the source's 368 K limit remains extrapolation. No chemistry law was
adjusted in these probes. Xiao's own modified Kent–Eisenberg model
(§2, Eqs. 1–15) correlates its effective dissociation constant with temperature
and physical CO₂ solubility. That fitted relation is not a replacement for
the retained thermodynamic dissociation law. These comparisons use the
experimental loading column, not Xiao's calculated loading column.

AARD is $100\langle|p_{\rm calc}/p_{\rm obs}-1|\rangle$; bias is the signed
mean of the same relative error. All 108 pressure states per probe returned
values. Their declared finite phase searches detected zero dense-liquid or
gas witnesses and zero unresolved states. This does not establish global
stability. The original pressure predictions replay within $10^{-8}$ relative
(or $10^{-8}$ Pa near zero).

| Representation and probe | Shared $k$ | Xiao AARD (%) | Xiao bias (%) | Ermatchkov AARD (%) | Ermatchkov bias (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 baseline | 0.727056 | 20.3976 | −20.3976 | 26.2084 | −18.8835 |
| A3, $k-0.1$ | 0.627056 | 10.5526 | −3.3441 | 23.1772 | −1.3759 |
| A3, $k+0.1$ | 0.827056 | 34.4541 | −34.4541 | 34.7715 | −32.9226 |
| A3, retained joint refit | 0.294490 | 19.1954 | −18.6376 | 20.7305 | −5.7513 |
| B1 baseline | 0.727056 | 28.2764 | −28.2066 | 19.1460 | +0.8939 |
| B1, $k-0.1$ | 0.627056 | 16.4205 | −11.9838 | 27.2756 | +23.2050 |
| B1, $k+0.1$ | 0.827056 | 41.4631 | −41.4631 | 23.3225 | −16.9997 |
| B1, retained joint refit | −0.086756 | 30.0501 | −30.0501 | 32.5173 | −31.2243 |

![The discrete pressure-error metrics show the opposing Ermatchkov consequences of a lower shared bicarbonate interaction. Circles denote A3, squares B1; each point summarizes the retained source rows for one declared probe, without interpolation. Measurement and parameter uncertainty are not propagated.](results/transfer-267/pressure-comparison.png)

The retained joint refits also changed MDEA-specific coordinates. They do not
isolate bicarbonate sensitivity. The separate frozen-endpoint $k\pm0.1$
calculations do. The 24.2% Ermatchkov criterion is a repository assessment
limit, not experimental uncertainty. A3 at $k-0.1$ enters that limit; B1 at the
same shared value leaves it. None of these cases eliminates the negative Xiao
mean bias in both representations while meeting the Ermatchkov criterion for
both.

### Consequences for the frozen MEA parameter record

Every tested shared value was evaluated on all 307 MEA fitted observations,
with every other parameter and law fixed. All 307 predictions were available
at each value. The original endpoint cost replays to $10^{-10}$ relative.
These costs use the existing observation scales and weights; they are not

### Testing the active parameter bounds

One matched refit per representation uses the original fitted observations,
weights and scales, starting from the selected endpoint. Shared values remain
at the MEA baseline. Only four finite search limits change: cation–CO₂ and
cation–water constant $k$ use [−0.6, 0.6], cation–bicarbonate uses [−1.2, 1],
and Born diameter uses [1.5, 8] Å. The other limits and nine-coordinate
parameterization are unchanged. Native fitting retains the 40-iteration and
2100-second limits and the original tolerances.

These intervals test whether artificial search limits control the comparison;
they are not measured physical parameter ranges. Uyan 2015 Eq. 7 gives
$u_{ij}=\sqrt{u_i u_j}(1-k_{ij})$. Requiring nonnegative unlike attraction
excludes $k>1$ under that interpretation. Positive component energies and
diameters are also necessary conditions. They do not establish parameter
identifiability or physical validation. The cation–water temperature law is
checked at 293.15 and 395 K, the endpoints of this assessment interval.

The A3 fit converges in 13 iterations, with weighted cost 396.38810 versus
403.71499 at the original endpoint. Its Ermatchkov AARD is 20.43947%, with
+5.24458% bias; Xiao AARD is 20.96662%, with −19.66526% bias and 17/20
underpredictions. The cation–water $k=-0.6$, cation–bicarbonate $k=-1.2$ and
Born diameter 8 Å reach the expanded bounds. Its cation–water law remains
below 1 at both temperature endpoints. Thus expanding the box changes the
pressure comparison but does not remove bound dependence or the Xiao miss.
Its finite full-state phase search covers 754 states, detects 35 gas-evolution
witnesses, and detects no dense-liquid split or unresolved state. These gas
witnesses are distinct from the rejected dense-liquid phase condition. [Fit, replay and phase evidence](results/transfer-267/A3-bounds/)
retain every original fitted group, native trial failure and phase classification.

The B1 expanded-bound fit converges in 5 iterations at cost
373.17470, versus 374.45201 originally. Its Xiao AARD/bias remain
28.02791% / −27.95981%; Ermatchkov gives 18.99988% / +0.10828%.
Its 754-state finite phase search detects 36 gas-evolution witnesses, no
dense-liquid split, and no unresolved state. Cation–bicarbonate $k=1$ and
Born diameter 8 Å remain bound-active.
Extending the former beyond 1 would leave the adopted nonnegative unlike-attraction
interpretation. Neither fit isolates the cation, and the pressure ranking remains
reversed between the sources. These two finite box extensions do not support
an unrestricted statement about every admissible parameterization.

Every original fitted property group remains in the objective. Their weighted
costs are retained below; heterogeneous groups must not be compared as equally
weighted physical errors. Fresh native-prediction replays reproduce weighted
residuals within $10^{-8}$ absolute and cost within $10^{-8}$ relative.

### The missing 333 K heat

The charged-molecule B1 native saturation-capped heat at 333.15 K, 60 wt% MDEA,
1121 kPa and source loading cap 0.811 mol/mol remains unavailable after
refining the loading search from the original 30 samples to 60 and 120 samples
over the same 0.05–1.50 mol/mol bounds. The native diagnostic cannot admit a
vapor-density branch: at the original grid it finds a stable root at
33402.24 mol/m³ above a negative-slope sample at 10464.56 mol/m³, with an
unexamined gap and unresolved slope reversals. Finer loading sampling changes
the failing density values but does not resolve branch admission. This is a
numerical search limitation; it does not show that absorption heat is
physically undefined.

| Control, at 60 wt% and 1121 kPa | 30-sample heat (kJ/mol CO₂) | 60-sample heat | 120-sample heat |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3, 333.15 K | −76.268595 | −76.268595 | −76.268595 |
| B1, 388.71 K | −64.128582 | −64.128582 | −64.128582 |

The controls' largest change is below $4\times10^{-9}$ J/mol CO₂. The separate
saturation diagnostic near 0.80691 mol/mol was not substituted for the native
observable. No complete two-observation B1 60 wt% heat AARD is calculated.
Sixty wt% remains a composition extrapolation. [The exact reproducer](results/transfer-267/heat-reproducer.json)
retains parameter documents, caloric and reaction declarations, all grids,
failure messages and the requested upstream check. The requested correction
must preserve the full-grid uniqueness check and both controls. The
[original wheel results](results/transfer-267/heat.json) separate the failure
from these useful control heat values.

The latest merged Engine main tested here is `4ffbb2b0825a28cdfa87dc333a586e641ff4c4b0`,
with wheel SHA-256 `40a58fc8f341f2ef4d9f26ae604cda93a5380e2a87073147bc2ba8efb17864b2`.
An unmodified archive of that fetched commit was built and installed in a separate
worktree environment. The [latest-wheel reproduction](results/transfer-267/heat-latest.json)
returns the same B1 333.15 K refusal on every grid. Both controls agree with the
original wheel within $1.4\times10^{-13}$ relative. The failure therefore persists
on that merged main commit. The combined [heat reproducer](results/transfer-267/heat-reproducer.json)
contains both wheel identities, all input documents, grids, outputs and the stated
correction criteria. The orchestrator owns the Engine request; this study has not
changed Engine source or adopted the diagnostic wheel.


For #255 stage 3, retain both cation representations and test the final MEA
shared values with these source-specific consequences visible. The small
bicarbonate decrease is a sensitivity direction for joint assessment, not a

Resolve the Engine heat search separately before reporting a complete B1
60 wt% heat statistic. No new parameter record is adopted.

## Issue 298: MDEA refits with the adopted shared MEA values

**The declared refits do not recover all required properties.** B1 recovers both pressure baselines; A3 recovers neither. Both selected records fail the Carson group-preservation rule. A3 also fails two outside-fit heat checks at 388.71 K and 60 wt% MDEA. This is the transfer penalty of the adopted shared set under this model, objective, bounds and declared starts, rather than a global impossibility result.

The historical costs reproduce after restoring the pre-0e216fe water ideal-gas calorics in scratch. The refits use current calorics and the pinned 391dfe5d wheel. Kuranov source rows 28 and 72 are excluded from both baselines and refits, leaving 278 fitted observations. The adopted R2 law is unchanged.

These are calibration and numerical verification results for the manuscript workflow comparison. They do not establish absorber suitability or parameter transferability. No parameters are adopted. Independent delivered-evidence review and investigator promotion remain pending.

### Limits and retained evidence


The two A3 outside-fit heat failures are concentration extrapolations at 388.71 K and 60 wt% MDEA. For the half-loading diagnostic, the calculated heat changes from −82.344969 to −85.682725 kJ/mol CO₂ against an observation of −63.3 kJ/mol, increasing absolute error by 3.337756 kJ/mol. For the capped integral heat, it changes from −74.141516 to −77.732589 kJ/mol, increasing absolute error by 3.591073 kJ/mol. Both increases exceed the permitted residual scale of 3.165 kJ/mol.

For B1 at 333.15 K, 60 wt% MDEA and 1.121 MPa, the capped heat remains unavailable at both baseline and refit: the original native search refuses the vapor branch at loading 1.45 mol/mol. No shortened grid or finite substitute heat is used, and no numerical heat-recovery claim is made for that row.

The two excluded Kuranov temperatures (393.17 and 393.16 K) exceed the adopted R2 upper limit of 393.15 K. No law was extended. Historical costs use 280 rows and are not directly comparable to the 278-row costs. Phase failure rejects an endpoint; unresolved numerical checks prevent a clean verdict. Neither establishes global impossibility of recovery. Active bounds and local Jacobian rank do not establish parameter identification. The 60 wt% comparisons remain concentration extrapolations. The original 30-node heat search over loading 0.05–1.50 mol/mol is preserved, including refusals. A historically unavailable B1 heat has no finite historical comparator.

F1.json owns qualification and provenance; attempts.json and each start directory own fit results; eligibility.json owns endpoint eligibility; selection.json freezes selection before pressure scoring; pressure-scores.json and gates.json own the comparisons. No source coefficients or Engine source were changed. The historical-water calculation is retained as logs/water-coefficient-confirmation.py and its row outputs, with coefficients recoverable from Git.

Execution: agent-heavy .venv/bin/python analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/scripts/continue_298.py runs the declared fits after historical confirmation; agent-heavy .venv/bin/python analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/scripts/assess_298.py runs the endpoint checks and assessments. The latter reuses retained phase calculations and applies the owner domain exclusion before freezing the selection.
